learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects of strength of materials regarding the behavior of real solids.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve strength of materials problems using established methods.
Be able to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in the field of elastic behavior of prismatic elements.
Be able to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs in elastic prismatic elements that meet specific requirements.
Have an understanding of the different methods in strength of materials and the ability to use them.
Be able to design and conduct strength of materials experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Have technical and laboratory competences in strength of materials.
Be able to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to solve strength of materials problems.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve strength of materials problems.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in strength of materials and their limitations.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
An adequate knowledge of their branch of engineering that includes some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of the different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competences.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.

syllabus_topics: Normal stresses: axial force and bending moment
Shear stresses: shear force and torsional moment
TOPIC 2: CALCULATION OF DISPLACEMENTS IN PRISMATIC ELEMENTS
assessment_rules: A final exam will be held, accounting for 60% of the final grade. For the continuous assessment grade to be considered in the final grade, a minimum score of 4.5 must be obtained in the final exam. Attendance and completion of the scheduled laboratory practices are mandatory to pass the course.
